Reports are tied to three filing dates per year and cover four-calendar-month periods, which is not quarterly.

instantiated_cells.justification: Section 101.72(B) sets filing dates (Jan/May/Sep), and §101.73(D) specifies each statement covers the preceding four-calendar-month period.

A legislative agent's expenditure statement must itemize reportable expenditures by recipient with total amount, description, approximate date, and related legislation/client (and similarly for meals once over $50), which is itemized reporting.
Legislative agents must file expenditure statements with updated registration statements due the last day of January, May, and September each year (three times annually), i.e., triannual.
Legislative agents must list specific bills or resolutions advocated in the updated registration statement and must report specific items of legislation associated with certain expenditures.

The expenditure-report definition expressly excludes 'the compensation paid to legislative agents,' and no provision shown requires legislative agents to disclose amounts of compensation received from employers.

instantiated_cells.justification: The statute requires reporting bills/resolutions advocated but does not require disclosure of specific lobbying contacts or communications.
Expenditures are linked to specific items of legislation 'if any,' but the statement does not require expenditures to be reported per issue/legislation as a mandatory categorization for all spending.
The initial registration statement must include 'a brief description of the type of legislation to which the engagement relates,' which is issue/subject-level disclosure.
Legislative agents must disclose a brief description of the type of legislation to which the engagement relates, which constitutes reporting general subjects of lobbying.

Expenditures include gifts, entertainment, lodging, and transportation, and when such expenditures are made for covered officials they must be reported with amount/description/date under §101.73(B)(2).

The statute does not require legislative agents to report indirect lobbying costs generally; employer office overhead is excluded and only defined 'expenditures' to/for covered officials are reportable.

Legislative agents file itemized expenditure statements and their registration identifies the employer/real party in interest, but the statute does not require disclosure of compensation received, so the regime still mandates itemized spending reports with employer identification and activity details.
The registration statement requires the legislative agent's name, business address, and occupation, but does not require a phone number.
Updated registration statements must list the specific bills or resolutions on which the agent actively advocated during the covered period.

The registration statement requires the employer's name and business address (and real party in interest if different) but does not require identifying whether the principal's business is public or private.
The statute requires the employer's and real party in interest's business addresses but does not require phone numbers for principals.
A legislative agent must file an initial registration statement for each engagement listing the employer (and real party in interest if different), thereby disclosing each principal represented.
The updated registration statement must list specific bills or resolutions, and expenditure statements must identify 'specific items of legislation, if any,' for which certain expenditures were made.

Compensation paid to legislative agents is expressly excluded from reportable 'expenditures' for employer statements, and the statute does not otherwise require reporting lobbying compensation as a direct cost.
A legislative agent's expenditure statement must show 'the total amount of expenditures made by the legislative agent during the reporting period.'

Legislative agents must file itemized expenditure statements and disclose employer and specific bills/resolutions, but no provision requires disclosure of compensation received, so the law provides itemized spending reports without compensation disclosure.

While legislative agents must file expenditure statements with each updated registration statement, the statute does not explicitly require a 'no spending/no activity' (zero) report when no expenditures occurred.

Reportable lobbying 'expenditures' are defined as those made to or for listed public officers/employees, and the statute does not include household/immediate family members of those officials as reportable recipients.
When expenditures trigger reporting, the legislative agent must provide recipient name, total amount, description, and approximate date, which constitutes itemized (not merely lump-sum) disclosure.
